findings.evidence: `nm -D --undefined-only runtime.so | grep pys` gives pys_obj_cmp, pys_obj_eq, pys_obj_repr (they are declared at runtime.c:854-856). `python3 jit_inproc.py t/jitme.exp.ll runtime.so init main` prints `python3: symbol lookup error: .../runtime.so: undefined symbol: pys_obj_repr` with rc=127. The fib/greet/checked steps with runtime.so work (first lookup 10.4 ms).

findings.claim: Two gaps in the in-process (python3) setup. python3.13 does not map libgcc_s, which the runtime needs for _Unwind_* and the 128-bit division helpers __divti3/__modti3/__udivti3, so it must be preloaded with RTLD_GLOBAL. python3.13 links libpython statically, so the CPython symbols are in the executable.
findings.evidence: `python3 jit_inproc_nogcc.py t/jitme.exp.ll runtime.o fib` fails with `JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ __udivti3, __divti3, _Unwind_GetLanguageSpecificData, _Unwind_ForcedUnwind, ... ]`, rc=1. `ldd /usr/bin/python3.13` lists only libm, libz, libexpat and libc. Counting 'libgcc_s' in /proc/self/maps of python3 gives 0.

findings.claim: When code is entered from CPython, an uncaught Pystachy exception terminates the whole Python process: throw_ falls back to uncaught(), which exits. Every entry point needs a catch-all wrapper.
findings.evidence: runtime.c:2315-2324. `python3 jit_inproc.py t/jitme.exp.ll runtime.o init boom` prints `ValueError: boom 1` and exits with rc=1; 'python continues' is never printed.

findings.claim: pys_init is not idempotent. Calling it a second time (once from the host, then again from @main) corrupts the heap, because gc_init unconditionally allocates a fresh page map while the free lists still point into the old chunks.
findings.evidence: runtime.c:312-316 (`if (!(pmap = calloc(1 << 18, sizeof *pmap))) oom();`). `PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1 python3 jit_inproc.py t/jitme.exp.ll runtime.o init greet checked main` makes main print `len(greet(1000)) = 1` and NUL bytes instead of `[P(1), P(2)]`. With a single init (`... runtime.o main`) under the same stress the output is correct.

findings.claim: When there is no single @main frame (extension or in-process mode), the GC's stack bottom can be the end of the main thread's stack (__libc_stack_end, or the [stack] end minus 64). The scan then also covers CPython's C frames. That was correct under PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1. Passing exactly the [stack] end crashed (rc=139), because gc_init adds 16 bytes and the scan reads past the mapping. Python's heap is still not a root: a Str whose only reference was its address in a Python variable was clobbered.
findings.evidence: runtime.c:312-314 (`gc_bottom = sb + 2 * sizeof(void *)`). jit_inproc.py first passed stack_top(): `PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1 ... init gcstress` gave rc=139. With stack_top() - 64 the output is `a Str held only by Python, after GCs: CLOBBERED b''`. The ext module passes `(char *)__libc_stack_end - 64`, and under PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1 `greet ok: True` holds for 3000 calls.

findings.claim: An AOT CPython extension module built from the same Pystachy IR works with python3. It is llvm-linked from the program IR, a C module stub (PyInit and METH_FASTCALL entries), pyshim.bc and runtime.bc, then built with clang -shared. Pystachy exceptions caught by Pystachy-written entry wrappers come out as OverflowError and ValueError in Python. Calls from other threads are refused. Per-call cost is about 47 ns, against about 270 ns through ctypes.
findings.evidence: ext/: `llvm-link-18 prog.pp.ll pysext.bc ../pyshim.bc ../runtime.bc -o all.bc && clang -O2 -shared -fPIC all.bc -o pysext$(python3.13-config --extension-suffix) -lm`. `python3 ext_test.py ext` prints `import ms 0.42 / fib(50) = 12586269025 / OverflowError from Pystachy: integer result does not fit in 64 bits / ValueError from Pystachy: boom 7 / greet ok: True / 100k calls fib(20): ms 4.7 / 100k calls CPython fibpy(20): ms 36.1 / from another thread: ["Pystachy's GC is single-threaded: main thread only"]`. The same results hold under PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=1.

findings.claim: In extension mode, a Pystachy print is lost when stdout is not a tty: pys_finish, which flushes Pystachy's write buffer, never runs inside a host process.
findings.evidence: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ext'); import pysext; print('py before'); pysext.hello(1); print('py after')" > hello.out` writes only `py before\npy after` (19 bytes); 'hello from pystachy 1' is missing. runtime.c:122 notes that 'every way out of the program runs it (lli skips atexit handlers)'.

findings.claim: Python's embedded initialization under both AOT and lli finds the system prefix. Py_InitializeEx(0) leaves Pystachy's SIGINT handler in place, and sys.argv is [''] unless the shim sets it.
findings.evidence: ./t/prefix_aot and lli-18 -load=... t/prefix.jit.bc both print `/usr/bin/python3 /usr [''] 3.13.16 None` (sys.executable, sys.prefix, sys.argv, version, signal.getsignal(SIGINT)).

implications_for_ffi: Recommendation: support both tiers through one mechanism, because the same C-ABI shim plus extern declarations worked unchanged in AOT and JIT. The AOT driver change is to add libpython's link flags to the final clang line (the `build` branch at pystachy.py:16649); the JIT driver change is to add `-load=libpythonX.so -extra-object=shim.o` to the lli line (pystachy.py:16670). No runtime.c changes are needed to call into CPython from a program.

Extend the existing runtime-mode extern path (pystachy.py:8015-8020, 10927-10944) to user programs instead of hand-editing IR. Two requirements: declare externs with unknown effects (FX 'U', i.e. may raise) so a call inside a try is always an invoke; the void-stub test shows the current inference is wrong for externs. Keep the existing ABI rule of int, float, str or None only (pystachy.py:9762-9770), with bool passed as int.

Keep the 'prints what CPython prints' contract with a bridge module (for example lib/cpython.py, a name I made up) whose CPython implementation is plain Python (importlib, getattr, call) and whose Pystachy implementation is externs into the shim. The bare `...` stubs from the spike return None under CPython and would break the contract.

Represent a CPython object as an opaque handle (an int, or a final class with one int field), with explicit ownership and refcounts taken in C. Release references with an explicit close, a `with` block, or a GC sweep of unreachable handles modelled on files_sweep. Without one of these, each dead wrapper leaks one reference (measured: 50,000 blocks).

Pystachy objects passed to CPython need a pin or handle table that mark_roots scans (runtime.c:161-170), released by the capsule destructor. Raw pointers in capsules are freed under GC stress. A handle table also suits the planned WebAssembly GC backend, which allows no raw pointers.

At every boundary crossing: flush Pystachy's stdout before calling into Python and flush sys.stdout before returning, or route one writer through the other. Register pys_finish with Py_AtExit in extension mode.

Python-to-Pystachy entries (callbacks or extension functions) need compiler-generated wrappers, all of which the spike wrote by hand: try/except that turns a Pystachy exception into PyErr_SetString plus an error return, or uncaught() exits the host process; a main-thread check (the GC is single-threaded, runtime.c:35); a one-time idempotent init, since pys_init run twice corrupts the heap; and a stack bottom covering the host's frames (__libc_stack_end).

The runtime calls three functions the program defines (pys_obj_eq/cmp/repr), so the runtime cannot be a standalone .so loaded before the program. Link it as an object in the JIT (the -extra-object or LLVMOrcLLJITAddObjectFile path) or as bitcode in AOT. Otherwise the runtime would have to call those three through function pointers registered at init.

In-process JIT inside CPython is feasible with no new dependency (ctypes plus the system libLLVM 18), at about 28.5 ms against about 42 ms for an lli subprocess. It needs libgcc_s preloaded with RTLD_GLOBAL and the runtime added as a precompiled object, not bitcode (735 ms). It is fragile: it pins the system libLLVM's exact version and needs ctypes prototypes for each C API function. AOT extension modules are much cheaper per call (about 47 ns against about 270 ns through ctypes) and start in 0.4 ms. The evidence therefore favours AOT for Python-to-Pystachy, with JIT as an option for embedding (Pystachy-to-Python) and for development.
open_questions: Untested: reference cycles that run through both heaps (Python object -> capsule -> Pystachy object -> handle -> Python object). Neither GC can see or collect them; a design would need tp_traverse on the handle wrappers or weak references.

Untested: free-threaded CPython 3.13t and sub-interpreters. The spike only refuses calls from non-main threads; whether the conservative stack scan is safe under PEP 703, or with the GIL released during Pystachy calls, is unknown.
Not done: building against the Stable ABI (Py_LIMITED_API / abi3). The shim uses PyErr_GetRaisedException (3.12+) and other non-limited calls; whether abi3 can cover it was not checked.

Signals were not tested in depth: Py_InitializeEx(0) left Pystachy's SIGINT handler in place, but how Ctrl-C behaves while executing inside Python code (KeyboardInterrupt delivery across the boundary) is unknown.

Not tested: what happens if two Pystachy extension modules, each carrying its own runtime and GC, load into one process. Python loads extensions RTLD_LOCAL, so their symbols should not clash, but objects cannot cross between them.

Not done: costing the str and int boundary semantics. Pystachy's str is byte-indexed UTF-8 and its int is 64-bit and checked, against CPython's code-point str and bignum int. The shim decodes str as UTF-8 with surrogateescape and raises OverflowError on large ints; whether that matches the docs/typed-ir.md §7.4 'boundary checks' intent was not decided.

Not measured: JITing several modules into one LLJIT session (one JITDylib per module, or name clashes on main and pys_obj_*), and the cost of adding a second module once LLJIT and the runtime are loaded.
